the k-means and SVM algorithms can be combined for the automatic annotation of unlabeled sensor data.

the proposed Multiple Pair-Frequency based cluster validation index can be used to validate the k-means cluster labels and the k-means clusters can be used to train the classifiers for the purpose of classifying “non-sensitive” data and “sensitive data”.
we have proposed a novel approach for automatically annotating unlabeled data collected from smartphone sensors and we have validated the proposed technique with a real-world dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic annotation and classification of unlabeled sensor data from mobile crowd sensing users.
the automatic annotation of unlabeled sensor data from motion and GPS sensors.
the automatic annotation of unlabeled sensor data and the validation of the generated clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed approach can automatically and effectively annotate unlabeled sensor data.
this paper has successfully demonstrated the automatic annotation of unlabeled sensor data from motion and GPS sensors.
the hybridized approach of machine learning is a better alternative for annotating unlabled sensor data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the unsupervised learning algorithm (clustering) is a good starting point for the automatic annotation of unlabeled sensor data while a supervised learning algorithm (classification) can be used for the classification of annotated data.

we have successfully demonstrated that the k-means unsupervised learning algorithm can be used for the automatic annotation of unlabeled sensor data, and the Multiple Pair-Frequency validation technique can be used for validating the clusters generated by the k-means technique.
the proposed technique can be used to detect sensitive location data of mobile users in crowd sensing applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed cluster validation index and the classifiers can be applied for the purpose of automatically annotating unlabeled data from smartphones’ motion and location sensors.
the proposed cluster validation index can be used to validate clusters generated from any unsupervised learning algorithm for any type of unlabeled data.
the proposed technique can be used to detect sensitive location information from smartphone sensors, and it can be extended for detecting other sensitive information.
